description: A stump with no tree behind it, walking on root-legs. It does not mind you coming. It minds you leaving.
lore: Every village that ever was had one: the stump at the wood's edge where you walked people to say goodbye. You carried their bag that far and no farther, and they sat on it to retie a boot, and then they went, and you stood by the stump until you could not see them. A thousand villages, a hundred thousand goodbyes, all of them remembered hard by the people left standing there — and in Nangijala that much remembering, pooled in one shape, eventually stands up.

So mind the one thing every handler tells you and no field guide bothers to: a Stumpling will let you walk right up. It goes for your back. The lashing starts when you turn and go, because going is the only thing that was ever done to it, and somewhere in all that borrowed remembering it has decided, wordlessly, with nobody inside it to decide, that this time it will not be left.

[[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] will not crack them. She does the trade's other work all day and charges double to anyone who brings her one of these still whole, hoping she'll change her mind. The stone inside is [[items/crimson_vein_mossy_stone|blood-natured]] — it feeds your wounds shut while you fight, holding on to you the way the stump holds on to everyone — and she says a thing that keeps its grip that well should be allowed to keep it. People assume she is joking. People have not watched her leave her smithy, at the end of a market day, by the long way around the one that stands at the east fence.
gm_notes: Worked example of the v2 register: ~230 words, a thing HAPPENS (it strikes when you leave), a named living NPC whose behaviour characterises both her and it, the stone folded in via a link instead of a closing essay. The goodbye-stump origin is a leaf-story — root-free, safe under churn.
